I reviewed the whole file. I also read the definitions of `normalizedCoordinates`, `affineCoordinatePoint` and `projectivizationToProj`. I checked the simp lemma `projectivizationToProj_mk` in `HomogeneousCoordinatePoint.lean`. I read the downstream use in `SymmetricAlgebraClosedPoint.lean` and the example in `examples/PointExamples.lean`.

The file has two simp lemmas, `projectivizationToClosedPoint_val` and `projectivizationEquivClosedPoints_apply`. Both are `rfl` lemmas that unfold a coercion to `projectivizationToProj x`. They point from the wrapper to the underlying map, so they do not loop. They do not compete with each other, because they are about different functions. They compose with the existing `@[simp]` lemma `projectivizationToProj_mk`, so `(projectivizationEquivClosedPoints (Projectivization.mk k a ha)).1` simplifies all the way to `homogeneousCoordinatePoint a ha`. A separate `_mk` lemma would therefore be redundant.

The private lemmas and the injectivity and surjectivity theorems are not simp candidates. Their hypotheses are non-trivial and they are used by explicit `rw` or `exact`. A new `projectivizationToProj_inj` iff lemma would have only speculative benefit, because no use in the sources needs one.

I could not run Lean. That leaves one small uncertainty: I did not check for simp-set interactions that depend on instances.
